transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. Thanks for making time for this readiness review. As you know, Press 5 has been throwing intermittent servo-drive alarms over the last two production weeks, and we do have a replacement servo retrofit kit available in the maintenance storeroom. The regular Saturday maintenance window runs 06:00 to 16:00, and I'll be making the final call on whether we take Press 5 offline for the retrofit. Before I finalize the work order, I want to hear from each of you -- controls engineering, production planning, safety, and quality -- on any relevant findings or concerns. Let's start with controls engineering: what are you seeing on the servo-drive side?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I completed a controls bench test this morning. The retrofit requires exactly 2 hours for controller-parameter backup and restoration, followed by exactly 6 hours of controlled commissioning. That's 8 hours total, which fits within the 06:00 to 16:00 Saturday window. I haven't attached the bench-test note to the work order yet, but I can do that right after this review.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I need to share some important scheduling information. I confirmed the released schedule this morning: 480 housings are due for Monday shipment. Press 2 can make exactly 240 of them on Saturday, but it's already scheduled for a separate job in that same production period. The remaining 240 must be assigned to Press 5 after the retrofit. I haven't updated the shared schedule yet because the maintenance decision was still open.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: I need to flag a safety item before we finalize this. I completed a Saturday arc-flash review for Press 5 yesterday, but I haven't entered it in the safety permit yet. The review requires a documented lockout with zero-energy verification by two authorized employees, and a 1.5-meter exclusion boundary around Press 5's electrical cabinet. This needs to be part of the work order and scheduled within the Saturday window before anyone touches that cabinet.
transcript.speaker: A4

transcript.text: I need to flag a critical quality requirement before we finalize this work order. My customer control-plan review requires exactly 20 first-off housings from the retrofitted press to receive dimensional and torque checks, with all remaining production held until Quality approves those results. I received the revised control plan last night but have not yet linked it to the press work order. This means after the retrofit is complete and commissioning is done, we need to produce 20 first-off parts, run them through dimensional and torque inspection, and hold further production until I sign off. That's going to eat into the time available for the 240 housings Monique mentioned.
transcript.speaker: A5

commitments.detail: Attach the controls bench-test note to the work order after this review.
Update the shared schedule to reflect 240 housings on Press 2 and 240 on Press 5 after retrofit and quality release.

Enter the Saturday arc-flash review into the safety permit, including documented lockout with zero-energy verification by two authorized employees and a 1.5-meter exclusion boundary around Press 5's electrical cabinet, all scheduled within the Saturday window before any cabinet work begins.
Link the revised customer control plan to the Press 5 work order, requiring 20 first-off housings to pass dimensional and torque checks with all remaining production held until Quality signs off.
